topic: FSRU vessel arrangement and current operational posture (2025-26 refresh)
wiki_text: The Paldiski FSRU consists of a reception-ready mooring quay and jetty at Pakrineeme (Paldiski), connected to the Balticconnector pipeline. It was conceived as the Estonian berth for the floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU) jointly chartered by Estonia and Finland. Excelerate Energy's 150,900-cbm FSRU 'Exemplar' was instead stationed at Inkoo, Finland, which became operational first; Paldiski has since served as a reception-ready backup. The Paldiski jetty/main platform was completed in 2022 and Estonia's state stockpiling agency ESPA purchased the LNG quay and port infrastructure from Alexela/Infortar for EUR 31.5 million (excl. VAT) in early 2023. As of mid-2026 no FSRU is berthed at Paldiski. GEM correctly omits a Paldiski-specific nameplate capacity because regasification capacity is provided by the shared vessel at Inkoo; no Paldiski-specific FSRU has been secured. The record leaves FloatingVesselName blank, consistent with no vessel being stationed at Paldiski.
source_notes: EUR 31.5M quay purchase corroborated by Argus, ERR, and ESPA's own announcement (three independent outlets). Exemplar (150,900 cbm) placement at Inkoo corroborated by Excelerate (sponsor) and LNG Prime, and independently by Offshore Energy/JPT-SPE. No GEM-derivative source used.

topic: JetGas Muuga liquefied-methane terminal — current build-out plan (2024-26)
wiki_text: The current Tallinn/Muuga LNG project is a small-scale liquefied-methane terminal to be built by JetGas OU near quay No. 33 in the eastern part of Muuga Harbour. On 18 November 2024, Port of Tallinn (Tallinna Sadam) signed a superficies (building-rights) agreement with JetGas OU covering ~7,000 m2 for a 30-year term. The plan is for up to five storage tanks built in stages, with a pipeline connecting to the quayline; the first tank is targeted for end-2027 and full build-out by 2030 at the latest. The facility is intended primarily for bioLNG and other methane fuels (including e-LNG/synLNG) to support transport-sector decarbonisation. The Port of Tallinn's official development announcement names JetGas OU as the developer and does not mention Liwathon E.O.S. (the GIE-listed operator, which is the renamed Vopak E.O.S. tied to the earlier defunct Muuga proposal). As of mid-2026 no FID or construction start has been reported; the Nov-2024 agreement remains the latest concrete step.
source_notes: Nov-2024 superficies agreement (30-yr, ~7,000 m2, up to five tanks, first tank end-2027, build-out by 2030) corroborated by Tallinna Sadam's GlobeNewswire release and independently by ERR (national broadcaster), MarineLink, and PortNews. Upgraded from single-source to >=2 independent non-GEM sources -> CONFIRMED.

topic: Permanent onshore Paldiski terminal (Baltic Gaas) — shelved/dormant status (2026 refresh)
wiki_text: The permanent onshore Paldiski LNG Terminal (Baltic Gaas, originally an Alexela Group subsidiary's project; Infortar joined in 2022) was envisioned as the second-phase permanent replacement for the first-phase FSRU/floating solution. The floating route prevailed: the shared FSRU was placed at Inkoo, Finland, and Estonia's ESPA bought the Paldiski quay in early 2023. The onshore permanent terminal has seen no activity for several years and is presumed shelved by inactivity (GEM ShelvedCancelledStatusType=inferred). A 2025-26 search found no revival or formal cancellation announcement, leaving the project a candidate for shelved->cancelled escalation in the next cycle.
source_notes: Shelved-by-inactivity is an inference (no discrete cancellation event). Only LNG Prime ('Infortar joins...') documents the project's last-active state off-GEM; the FSRU-route-prevailed framing is corroborated by the quay-purchase sources cited on the Paldiski FSRU record. Dropped the prior unverified '2017 CEF funding denied' claim, which no independent non-GEM source could confirm. Remains single-source for the onshore project itself -> UNVERIFIED.
